On Mon, 26 Oct 2026 at 10:03, jordan_blake@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Sara — looping in security and ops. High level: we can provide most artifacts but retention policies differ by artifact and deployment mode...

Quick technical notes / tradeoffs (ETA & constraints):

1) KMS rotation provenance for Private BYOK
- Current state: rotation timestamps and key identifiers are logged in control-plane telemetry (customer-managed key references). However, the full rotation-proof chain (signed rotation statements) is generated only when the KMS provider supports export APIs (limited by HSM vendors).
- Work required: build an export shim + canonicalization routine to generate a signed rotation proof bundle. Estimate: 3 sprints (2 backend eng, 1 infra). Risk: requires coordination with customer KMS vendor for archive format.

2) SSO session assertions / long-term retention
- We can increase assertion retention to 1 year for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we currently cap at 90 days to limit storage and PII surface. Enabling longer storage requires an opt-in and updated DPA text. Ops impact: +15% storage for SSO indices.

3) API request logs & payloads
- We already store metadata (headers, request id, timestamp) for 180 days. Storing request bodies/payloads is opt-in and flagged as PII-intensive. If EdgeHealth requires payloads, we need an exception flow and data handling process. Estimate: 2 sprints to add opt-in plumbing + retention TTL controls.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix that maps each artifact to: storage location, retrieval API, export format, and estimated engineering lead.

Irene Choi
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
